title.narrative: DRA ACJR Indonesia 2025 – Aceh floods/cyclone

description.narrative: On 26 November, Tropical Cyclone Senyar caused catastrophic flooding across Aceh and West/North Sumatra, displacing over 884,889 people across 2,186 evacuation centers and severely damaging 158.000 houses and 219 health and 581 education facilities, resulting in 990 deaths. The Yayasan Plan (YPII) Emergency Response Team has been deployed since 29 November and conducted an RNA between 2–4 December in Aceh, complemented by secondary data from BNPB and IHCP Situation Reports. In target districts Aceh Timur, Langsa, and Bener Meriah, RNA findings confirm critical unmet needs. WASH conditions are severely inadequate, with no gender-segregated toilets, long queues, reliance on contaminated water for washing, absence of waste management and lack of MHM supplies. Over 80% of HHs relied on bottled water for drinking while using contaminated floodwater due to broken water infrastructure. HHs report a complete loss of income and limited purchasing power. The RNA confirmed increasing functionality of markets but with limited stock, which Plan estimates will allow MPC to be effective from early January, while before that in-kind is key. Protection risks are acute. No formal protection mechanisms or complaint channels exist in the targeted camps. Children lack structured activities and psychosocial support, boys are engaged in unsafe adult tasks, and women and girls face heightened safety and dignity risks due to non-segregated facilities. PwD and the elderly experience exclusion due to inaccessible camp layouts. Pre-existing GBV prevalence (967 GBV cases in Aceh Jan.-Oct. 2025) further increases protection risks during displacement. While government assistance covers food, basic shelter and some EiE/Health, significant gaps remain in WASH, integrated protection services, MPC, and coordinated community engagement. Plan and CMC will address these gaps through a multisectoral response in close coordination with other DRA partners and the local authorities.

SUMMARY: On 26 November, Tropical Cyclone Senyar caused catastrophic flooding across Aceh and West/North Sumatra, displacing over 884,889 people across 2,186 evacuation centers and severely damaging 158.000 houses and 219 health and 581 education facilities, resulting in 990 deaths. While government assistance covers food, basic shelter and some EiE/Health, significant gaps remain in WASH, integrated protection services, MPC, and coordinated community engagement. Plan and CMC will address these gaps through a multisectoral response in close coordination with other DRA partners and the local authorities together with other 5 DRA partners and 14 LPs. Plan is in the lead of this response.

The response will be implemented jointly by Plan & CMC, combining YPII’s technical emergency response capacity with CMC’s deep community access and cultural knowledge. This approach, designed jointly by the partners, ensures effective delivery of integrated WASH, Protection, and MPC in Aceh’s conservative Islamic context, where gender norms and local leadership strongly influence access. Both partners will implement WASH, protection & MPC, each in charge of different sub-districts, but guided by Plan’s technical experts and the systems put in place by YPII’s overall response. CMC is an existing partner and capacity building will be continued (e.g. on GBV and referral mechanisms). They will receive 35,4% of the budget and 6% ICR. The MPCA modality will prioritise mobile money transfers where network coverage permits, with bank agent payments or manual cash distributions (supported by female volunteers) as contingency options. The team already has contracts in place with providers for WASH activities. As for collaboration with other JR members, all members coordinated extensively during the design and decided to primarily focus on avoiding overlap. Plan ended up selecting (sub-)districts that other members had no access to, thus focussing on more remote areas of central Aceh to leverage Plan’s access. YPII also already collaborates with Save the Children (and local NGO Yayasan Geutanyoe), whose existing case management systems complement Plan and CMC’s proposed intervention.

The response will target 16,870 people across three districts in Aceh, including 40% children and 60% adults. The design prioritises vulnerable groups identified through the RNA, including children, women, persons with disabilities, GBV survivors, unaccompanied and separated minors, pregnant and lactating women and orphans. Interventions are aligned with YPII’s Child Rights and Gender Equality and Inclusion framework and include survivor-centered GBV services, inclusive support for persons with disabilities, targeted MPCA and health interventions for women and elderly persons, and family tracing and documentation support for separated children. A conflict-sensitive, community-validated approach, grounded in CMC’s expertise in child protection and psychosocial support, ensures culturally appropriate, trauma-informed assistance that promotes protection, dignity, and gender equality specific for the Aceh context.

YPII and CMC are already implementing emergency response activities, focusing in particular on NFI distributions due to market dysfunctionality in the early days of the response. YPII’s RNA suggests that market functionality is improving, making MPC most important from early January. Plan and CMC will thus continue WASH activities immediately, with first DRA distributions (water trucking) planned for December 22nd. The hygiene promotion and Protection activities will be conducted throughout the project. Beneficiary selection will also commence immediately, with the intention of completing all distributions before the start of Ramadan. PDMs will be conducted 2 weeks after cash transfers. Plan and CMC plan to wrap up most activities, including the protection elements, by the end of the rainy season (mid-March 2026), focussing afterwards only on handovers and strengthening capacities of volunteers, local government actors and the CBCPs to ensure community ownership.
